paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: load MCP tool definitions on demand with tool_search
# dsh-tool-search
English | Português
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps large tool sets, such as many MCP servers, out of every model r
equest. Tool definitions are loaded on demand with a `tool_search` tool.
With many MCP servers configured, every request carried hundreds of definitions the agent never used
. In one measured native desktop session, 480 tools weighed 396 KB of JSON per request, and 352 KB o
f that was MCP definitions. With this plugin the model sees a short list of tool groups plus `tool_s
earch`, and the tools it loads are declared from its next step.
Deferred tools stay registered and executable. Only the declaration size of each request changes. De
ferral is presentation, not access control; use the harness's own tool restrictions to forbid a tool
erral is presentation, not access control; use the harness's own tool restrictions to forbid a tool.
## Install
The module has no package imports and reads everything from the Cordis `ctx`, so one file mounts by
absolute path. Add a row to your profile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The host caches plugin modules, so restart it after you change the file. Removing the row restores t
he full declarations.
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `defer` | required | `*`-wildcard patterns over complete tool names. Matching tools are withheld u

ntil loaded. |
| `keep` | `[]` | Patterns that are never withheld, even when `defer` matches. |
| `m
axResults` | `8` | Most tools one keyword search loads. |
An empty `defer` list, an empty pattern, or a non-positive `maxResults` fails when the plugin loads.
## How it works
The model calls `tool_search` with `query` keywords, exact `names`, or both. Keyword search ranks un
loaded deferred tools by how many query terms their names and descriptions contain (name hits count
more) and loads the best `maxResults`. A name that no pattern defers is reported as already loaded;
an unknown name is reported as unknown.
- **Native mode.** The plugin removes deferred entries from the tools of `system-prompt/assemble` an

d adds a catalog section that lists each deferred group once with its tool count.
- **PTC mode.** Th
e plugin rewrites the generated `tools:sdk` section, removing deferred members from `ToolArgsMap` an
d `ToolOutputMap`. The model calls `await tools.tool_search({ query })` inside `run_code`. A layout

it does not recognize is left unfiltered, with one warning in the log.
- **Per agent.** Loading is p
er agent. A subagent starts with nothing loaded. A resumed native session keeps the tools its last l
ogged request header declared, provided that header already declared `tool_search`. A resumed PTC se
r declared, provided that header already declared `tool_search`. A resumed PTC session starts empty.
## Compatibility
Verified on DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2. Newer releases moved tool declarations out of the `syste
m-prompt/assemble` assembly into the provider. On such a release native deferral is inactive: the pl
ugin leaves the assembly untouched and logs one warning (`native deferral is inactive`) instead of f
ailing prompt assembly. The PTC filter depends on the member layout that the SDK generator emits.
## Known limits

- Deferral hides declarations only. A model that guesses an unloaded tool name can still call it.
-

Loaded tools are never unloaded within a session.
- Keyword ranking is plain term containment, with

no stemming or synonyms.
- Loading a tool changes the tool list (native) or the SDK text (PTC), so t
he cached request prefix after that point is rewritten on the next request. Loading related tools in

one search limits the rewrites.
- In PTC mode `tool_search` runs inside `run_code`, which costs one
program per search.
